subject.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback

question: Should `secrets.ref_env_fallback_used` warn whenever a configured SecretRef fails and an existing environment credential keeps the active surface working, or should that intentional compatibility fallback use narrower scope or lower severity?
rationale: The implementation can detect the state safely, but whether every active fallback represents a warning-worthy security boundary is an operator-policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Keep the warning
options.body: Treat every active configured-ref-to-environment fallback as warning-worthy because it hides a broken intended secret source.

options.title: Narrow the warning
options.body: Warn only for selected security-critical credential surfaces or when the configured provider differs from the fallback source.

options.title: Report as information
options.body: Keep visibility but classify intentional compatibility fallback as informational unless strict policy is enabled.

recommendation.title: Keep the warning
recommendation.body: Treat every active configured-ref-to-environment fallback as warning-worthy because it hides a broken intended secret source.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans the plugin trust model, authentication compatibility, and operator-facing security policy, where their recent history is broadest.
